stories.headline: Trump administration asks OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6 release, vetting customers one by one

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration asked OpenAI to limit the release of GPT-5.6 to only a small set of government-approved partners before any wider release, citing security concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration has asked OpenAI to limit the release of its next model, GPT-5.6, to only a small set of government-approved partners before any wider release, citing security concerns, according to a source familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman told employees Wednesday in a company Q&A that GPT-5.6 would launch in limited preview to a small group of enterprise customers, with the government approving access customer by customer during the preview period.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman told employees Wednesday in a company Q&A that it would release GPT-5.6 in limited preview form... During that preview period, the Trump administration itself would reportedly approve access for customers on a case-by-case basis.

key_facts.fact: The request for a staggered release came from conversations with the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy.
key_facts.excerpt: The request for a staggered release came from conversations with two key government agencies, the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

key_facts.fact: Altman discussed GPT-5.6 with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday; a source said the government intervened because the model has 'Mythos-like' capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman discussed GPT-5.6 with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday... The source said the government intervened because GPT-5.6 has 'Mythos-like' capability.

key_facts.fact: Altman said in the memo this is 'not our preferred long term model' and that he hopes to release GPT-5.6 more broadly a 'couple of weeks later'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We've made clear to the US government that this is not our preferred long term model"... hopefully followed a "couple of weeks later" by a more general release of the 5.6 model.

key_facts.fact: The move follows an AI security executive order Trump signed earlier this month directing agencies to stand up a voluntary testing protocol for AI companies before releasing new models.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump signed an executive order earlier this month asking AI companies to participate in a voluntary federal review of their more powerful models before they are publicly released.

stories.headline: OpenAI leans toward delaying IPO to 2027 as Altman holds firm on $1T valuation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is leaning toward holding off its IPO until 2027, according to the New York Times citing three people involved in the company's deliberations.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is leaning towards holding off on an initial public offering until 2027, the New York Times reported, citing three people involved in the company's deliberations.

key_facts.fact: The company had hired bankers and lawyers eyeing an IPO as soon as the third or fourth quarter of this year, with Altman pushing advisers to find a way to value OpenAI at $1 trillion, up from its last private valuation of $730 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The maker of ChatGPT hired bankers and lawyers with an eye toward a public offering as soon as the third or fourth quarter of this year... Sam Altman... pushed those advisers to find a way for the start-up to be valued at $1 trillion, up from the company's last private valuation of $730 billion.

key_facts.fact: Advisers presented executives with two options — wait until 2027 to go public at $1 trillion, or lower the valuation for a quicker IPO — and Altman called any change to the trillion-dollar valuation a 'nonstarter'.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's advisers presented company executives with the option of waiting until 2027 to go public with a $1 trillion valuation, or lower the targeted valuation for a quicker I.P.O. Mr. Altman... responded that any change to the trillion-dollar valuation was a nonstarter.

key_facts.fact: Bankers cautioned that recent volatility in tech stocks and in SpaceX's shares after its record IPO could dampen retail-investor enthusiasm for an OpenAI offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Bankers advising the ChatGPT maker on its IPO plans cautioned that recent volatility in tech stocks, as well as in SpaceX's shares following its record IPO, could dampen enthusiasm from retail investors for OpenAI's offering.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI filed confidentially for an IPO with the SEC, disclosing the move in a June 9 statement that said it had not decided on timing.
key_facts.excerpt: The company filed confidentially for an IPO with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, according to a statement on June 9. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while..."

key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, General Intuition said it raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation... The round brings General Intuition's total disclosed funding to $454 million, after the $134 million round it raised at launch last October.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Nico Rosberg, and researchers at Google DeepMind and MIT.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition's latest round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Nico Rosberg, and researchers at Google DeepMind and MIT.

stories.headline: California launches first US tracker linking AI exposure to unemployment claims

key_facts.fact: California launched the California AI-Unemployment Tracker (CAIT) on June 25, a first-in-the-nation tool linking unemployment-insurance claims with measures of occupational AI exposure, updated monthly.
key_facts.excerpt: A new, first-in-the-nation tracker launched today in California... The California AI-Unemployment Tracker (CAIT) links unemployment insurance (UI) claims with measures of occupational AI exposure to monitor labor market changes as they unfold.

key_facts.fact: As of May 2026, researchers found no evidence of a statewide surge in layoffs among workers in highly AI-exposed occupations.
key_facts.excerpt: as of May 2026 there is no evidence of a statewide surge in layoffs among workers in highly AI-exposed occupations, though early signs of disruption are emerging among specific groups of workers, industries, and regions.

key_facts.fact: Early signs of disruption emerged: UI claims rose among college-educated workers in high-AI-exposure occupations and among high-exposure workers in the San Francisco Bay Area.
key_facts.excerpt: Unemployment insurance claims rose among college-educated workers in occupations with high exposure to AI, as well as those in occupations with high AI exposure in the San Francisco Bay area.

key_facts.fact: The tracker was developed by Gov. Newsom's office, the Employment Development Department, and the nonpartisan California Policy Lab at UCLA, under a May executive order on AI workforce disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: The California AI-Unemployment Tracker was developed with the California Policy Lab at UCLA and the Employment Development Department... Newsom issued an executive order in May aimed at preparing California workers, small businesses and communities for potential job disruption driven by AI.

key_facts.fact: More than 121,000 tech workers have been laid off this year per a global tracker run by startup founder Roger Lee, though not all of those layoffs are AI-related.
key_facts.excerpt: This year alone, more than 121,000 tech workers have been laid off, according to a global tracker from startup founder Roger Lee. While not all of those layoffs are AI-related, behemoths like Meta, Cisco and Microsoft have laid off thousands.

stories.headline: Onsemi to buy Synaptics in ~$7B all-stock deal to expand into physical AI

key_facts.fact: ON Semiconductor (onsemi) agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction with a total enterprise value of approximately $7 billion, its largest acquisition to date.
key_facts.excerpt: onsemi has agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $7 billion.

key_facts.fact: Synaptics shareholders will receive a fixed 1.350 onsemi shares per Synaptics share, a roughly 19% premium to the two stocks' 10-day volume-weighted average prices, giving Synaptics holders about 12% of the combined company.
key_facts.excerpt: Synaptics shareholders will receive 1.35 shares of onsemi common stock for each Synaptics share, representing a roughly 19% premium... The transaction would give Synaptics shareholders about 12% ownership of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.

key_facts.fact: The combination is intended to position onsemi at the center of 'Physical AI,' with potential to expand its total addressable market by $30 billion to $243 billion by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: the potential to expand onsemi's TAM by $30 billion to $243 billion by 2030.

key_facts.fact: The deal, unanimously approved by both boards, is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal has been unanimously approved by both companies' boards and is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval, regulatory clearances and customary closing conditions.

key_facts.fact: onsemi expects the acquisition to be accretive to adjusted earnings per share within 18 months of closing and to drive about $200 million in annual synergies; ON shares fell about 7.3% after hours to $110.12.
key_facts.excerpt: accretive to adjusted per-share earnings within 18 months of closing, adding that it will drive an expected $200 million in annual synergies... Shares of ON Semiconductor fell 7.3% to $110.12 after hours.

key_facts.fact: CEO Hassane El-Khoury said the deal adds Synaptics' Edge AI compute, human-machine interface and wireless connectivity to onsemi's power and sensing portfolio, targeting autonomous driving, robotics and AR/VR.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker also aims to capture growth from Synaptics' human-machine interface business and its broader technology and R&D in robotics and humanoid markets, El-Khoury said.

stories.headline: Apple raises Mac and iPad prices as AI memory shortage hits consumer tech

key_facts.fact: Apple raised prices across Macs, iPads, HomePods and Vision Pro on June 25, saying it could no longer shield customers from soaring memory and storage costs driven by the AI data-center buildout; the iPhone was left unchanged for now.
key_facts.excerpt: Amid a worldwide memory shortage driven by the AI buildout, Apple is raising prices of its Mac and iPad lineups... For the moment, there is no rise in iPhone prices.

key_facts.fact: Apple said in a statement: 'We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly. We have shielded our customers from these increases so far, but we have now reached a point where we need to begin raising prices.'
key_facts.excerpt: We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly. We have shielded our customers from these increases so far, but we have now reached a point where we need to begin raising prices on a number of products, including today's increases for iPad and Mac.

key_facts.fact: Specific increases included the MacBook Neo starting at $699 (up from $599), MacBook Air at $1,299 (up from $1,099), MacBook Pro with 1TB at $1,999 (up from $1,699), and the iPad Air 128GB at $749 (up from $599).
key_facts.excerpt: MacBook Neo now starts at $699 (up from $599), while MacBook Air now starts at $1299 (up from $1099). Other impacted products include MacBook Pro, iPad, iPad Air, and many more.

key_facts.fact: DRAM prices rose as much as 98% in Q1 2026 and are set to jump another 58% to 63% in the current quarter, per TrendForce, a surge dubbed 'RAMageddon'; memory makers like Micron have prioritized AI chipmakers such as Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Prices of dynamic random access memory... rose as much as 98 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and are set to jump by another 58 per cent to 63 per cent in the current quarter, according to industry tracker TrendForce.

key_facts.fact: Data centers are expected to consume as much as 70% of total memory production in 2026, leaving phone and PC makers competing for the remainder.
key_facts.excerpt: By one widely cited estimate, data centres are expected to consume as much as 70% of total memory production in 2026... For every ten chips coming off a line, seven head to server farms.

stories.headline: US Commerce signs $250M CHIPS deal with Friedland's I-Pulse for silicon-carbide chips

key_facts.fact: The Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research & Development Office signed a definitive agreement with I-Pulse for a $250 million award under the CHIPS and Science Act to develop novel silicon-carbide (SiC) power semiconductors.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research & Development Office today announced the signing of a definitive agreement with I-Pulse for a $250 million award under the CHIPS and Science Act.

key_facts.fact: I-Pulse, co-founded by mining billionaire Robert Friedland (CEO) and Laurent Frescaline (CTO), will develop high-temperature, high-current, high-voltage solid-state SiC switches for uses including underground mining, manufacturing, defense systems and geothermal drilling.
key_facts.excerpt: I-Pulse Co-founders Robert Friedland, CEO, and Laurent Frescaline, CTO, announced today a definitive agreement... commercialize cutting-edge, high-temperature, high-current, high-voltage solid-state switches. These switches have a multitude of applications including underground mining, rock crushing, manufacturing, and defense systems.

key_facts.fact: In connection with the award, the Department received a minority, non-controlling equity stake in I-Pulse.
key_facts.excerpt: In connection with the award, the Department received a minority, non-controlling equity stake in I-Pulse, which enhances the benefit to the U.S. taxpayer.

key_facts.fact: The program will be led by I-Pulse's Albuquerque, New Mexico team near Sandia National Laboratories and the Air Force Research Laboratory; the company also has facilities in Detroit and Toulouse, France.
key_facts.excerpt: The program would be led by the Albuquerque team, near Sandia National Laboratories and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory, and would involve U.S. national laboratories, universities and specialized manufacturers.

key_facts.fact: Friedland said the funding will advance geothermal technology, arguing 'the limiting factor in artificial intelligence is clean energy... The best answer is geothermal'; I-Pulse investors include Rio Tinto and Newmont and it is 'likely to be a public company in a few years.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The limiting factor in artificial intelligence is clean energy, and you can't do AI with solar or wind. The best answer is geothermal.'... Closely held I-Pulse exceeded a $1 billion valuation a decade ago and is 'likely to be a public company in a few years,' Friedland said. Investors include large miners such as Rio Tinto Group and Newmont Corp.

stories.headline: Apple to skip high-end M6 chips, jump to AI-focused M7 line in 2027

key_facts.fact: Apple plans to release a base M6 chip as early as this year but has canceled the M6 Pro and M6 Max; the next Pro and Max chips will arrive in the M7 generation, marking the first Apple silicon line without a Pro or Max variant since 2020, per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple plans to release an M6 chip for entry-level Macs as soon as this year, but it has canceled plans for higher-end M6 Pro and M6 Max chips. Instead, Apple's next Pro and Max chips will be part of its M7 chip lineup.

key_facts.fact: The base M7 is expected in the first half of 2027, with the M7 Pro and M7 Max at the end of 2027 and the M7 Ultra in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The base M7 chip is reportedly set for 'as early as the first half of next year.' The faster M7 Pro and M7 Max are slated for the end of next year, followed by the M7 Ultra in 2028.

key_facts.fact: The M7 line is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing, with the base M7 supporting about 240 GB/s of memory bandwidth, up from 153 GB/s on the M5.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The M7 line is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing,' Bloomberg reports. 'The base version is slated to support about 240 gigabytes per second of memory bandwidth.'

key_facts.fact: The base M6 (codenamed Komodo/H18G) is being tested in an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, with ~200 GB/s bandwidth and up to 12 GPU cores (vs 10 on the base M5).
key_facts.excerpt: The base M6 chip is reportedly being tested in an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro. The chip is internally known as Komodo or H18G. It is expected to improve memory bandwidth to around 200 GB/s... Apple has reportedly tested configurations with up to 12 GPU cores, up from 10 cores on the base M5.

key_facts.fact: Apple still plans an M5 Ultra chip as early as this year for a new Mac Studio, with around 36 CPU cores and 80 GPU cores.
key_facts.excerpt: The company introduced the M5 Pro and Max chips earlier this year, and we expect to see the M6 announced for its entry-level MacBooks before the end of 2026.

stories.headline: Cargo ship attacked near Oman; UN pauses Hormuz evacuation as oil jumps 2%

key_facts.fact: A cargo ship was struck by an 'unknown projectile' 7.5 nautical miles (14km) southeast of Oman's port of Dahit on Thursday June 25, damaging its bridge with no casualties reported.
key_facts.excerpt: The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Thursday that a ship had been struck 7.5 nautical miles southeast of Oman's port of Dahit by 'an unknown projectile'. No casualties were reported.

key_facts.fact: The UN's International Maritime Organization paused its plan to evacuate more than 11,000 stranded seafarers and around 600 ships from the Strait of Hormuz after the attack; some 57 ships carrying ~1,100 seafarers had passed through under the plan as of Thursday morning.
key_facts.excerpt: The International Maritime Organization announced a plan earlier this week to evacuate around 11,000 seafarers from the region... As of Thursday morning, data from the U.N. shipping agency showed some 57 ships carrying an estimated 1,100 seafarers had passed through the strait under the plan.

key_facts.fact: The attacked vessel was the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely, owned by Evergreen, which did not transit under the IMO evacuation framework and continued through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Maritime risk management firm Vanguard said the ship, the Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely, continued through the strait despite the attack... the vessel that was attacked 'did not transit under IMO's evacuation framework'.

key_facts.fact: A US official told MS Now that Iran was behind the attack; Iran's military had warned vessels against using the southern route approved by the IMO.
key_facts.excerpt: The pause follows a container ship being struck by an unknown projectile near the coast of Oman on Thursday, with a U.S. official telling MS Now that Iran was behind the attack.

key_facts.fact: Oil rose more than 2% on Thursday June 25: Brent settled up $1.52 (2.1%) at $75.26 a barrel and WTI rose $1.58 (2.3%) to $71.92; US gasoline futures jumped about 5%.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures rose $1.52, or 2.1%, to settle at $75.26 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude rose $1.58, or 2.3%, to settle at $71.92. ... U.S. gasoline futures jumped about 5%, while U.S. diesel gained about 4%.

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday both crude benchmarks had closed at their lowest since February 27, the day before the war began, after Hormuz shipments rose to their highest since the start of the conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, both crude benchmarks closed at their lowest since February 27, the day before the war began as crude shipments through the strait rose to their highest since the start of the war.

stories.headline: EU gives final approval to US trade pact, locking in 15% tariff on its exports

key_facts.fact: The European Council on Thursday June 25 gave final approval to the EU-US trade pact, removing remaining EU customs duties on US industrial goods in exchange for a 15% tariff on European exports.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Union (EU) on Thursday gave its final approval to the trade pact with the US, thereby removing the remaining customs duties on US industrial goods in exchange for a 15 percent tariff on European exports.

key_facts.fact: The deal formalizes the framework von der Leyen and Trump reached a year ago and will enter into force once published in the EU Official Journal, expected before July 4, the deadline Trump set with a threat to raise tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement will enter into force once it is published in the Official Journal of the EU, a procedure expected to be completed in the coming days, before July 4, the deadline set by Trump, who has threatened to raise tariffs if the EU fails to meet the deadline.

key_facts.fact: The 15% ceiling replaces the 25% tariff Trump had intended to impose; the EU added safeguards to suspend the deal if the US imposes tariffs above 15% on steel and aluminum derivatives by Dec 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The EU has granted tariff preferences to the US in exchange for Trump accepting a 15 percent tariff on European products, instead of the 25 percent he had intended to impose... The agreement may also be suspended if, by Dec. 31, 2026, the US imposes a tariff exceeding 15 percent on products derived from steel and aluminum.

key_facts.fact: The EU also extended tariff suspension to lobster imports and granted preferential access to certain US seafood and non-sensitive agricultural products; the agreement is set to terminate Dec 31, 2029 unless renewed.
key_facts.excerpt: The bloc is also extending the tariff suspension to lobster imports and granting preferential access to other types of US seafood and non-sensitive agricultural products... the EU has decided to terminate the agreement on Dec. 31, 2029.

key_facts.fact: The Council adopted two regulations linked to the EU-US Joint Statement of August 21, 2025, completing the bloc's legislative process.
key_facts.excerpt: In a statement, the [Council] adopted the two regulations linked to the EU-US Joint Statement of August 21, 2025, completing the bloc's legislative process.

stories.headline: NATO's Rutte says alliance will unveil tens of billions in defense contracts at Ankara summit

key_facts.fact: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Thursday June 25 the alliance will announce 'tens of billions of dollars' in new defense contracts at the July 7-8 summit in Ankara, Turkey.
key_facts.excerpt: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Thursday that the alliance will unveil tens of billions of dollars in new defense contracts at next month's summit in Turkiye's capital, Ankara... 'We will announce tens of billions of dollars of new contracts,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Rutte said allies are on a 'trajectory' to reach the defense spending goal agreed last year of 5% of GDP by 2035, with the summit focused on delivering on pledges.
key_facts.excerpt: The summit will underscore that after years of underinvestment, allies are on a 'trajectory' to reaching a defense spending goal agreed upon last year of 5% of GDP by 2035, said Rutte.

key_facts.fact: The draft summit declaration is expected to confirm 70 billion euros in military aid for Ukraine, with at least the same amount pledged for the following year, without US participation.
key_facts.excerpt: In the draft statement, allies are expected to confirm 70 billion euros in military aid for Ukraine and pledge at least the same amount for the following year. The United States will not take part in this funding.

key_facts.fact: The declaration will reaffirm Article 5, again describe Russia as a long-term threat, and call on Iran to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz as an 'olive branch' to Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: the draft declaration will reaffirm allies' commitment to Article 5 on collective defense and again describe Russia as a long-term threat... allies call on Iran to ensure freedom of navigation in this key trade route. Diplomats describe this as an 'olive branch' to Trump.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will attend the summit, which will reaffirm NATO's support for Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy will attend the summit, which will reaffirm NATO's support for Ukraine in its more than four-year-old battle against Russian occupation forces.

stories.headline: Binance to halt crypto services for EU clients from July 1 after MiCA license setback

key_facts.fact: Binance said Thursday June 25 it will suspend services in several European countries from next week after failing to secure regulatory approval to operate in the EU before the June 30 MiCA deadline.
key_facts.excerpt: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said Thursday it will suspend services in several European countries from next week as it has been unable secure regulatory approval to operate in the European Union.

key_facts.fact: Binance told clients it had withdrawn its MiCA license application in Greece (the Hellenic Capital Market Commission) and would apply in another EU country, not yet named.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance has withdrawn its MiCA license application in Greece and confirmed it will seek authorization in a different EU member state... The target jurisdiction remains undisclosed.

key_facts.fact: 'Binance France is no longer in a position to accept new clients and from July 1, 2026, will no longer [provide] crypto asset services in France,' it told clients; similar emails were sent to other affected EU markets.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Binance France is no longer in a position to accept new clients and from July 1, 2026, will no longer crypto asset services in France,' the company said in an email to clients on Wednesday. 'This is not specific to France, similar communications have been sent to affected users in other EU markets.'

key_facts.fact: Gillian Lynch, Binance's head of Europe and the UK, told Reuters the exchange is 'not leaving Europe' and would pursue authorization in another EU jurisdiction.
key_facts.excerpt: Gillian Lynch, Binance's head of Europe and the United Kingdom, told Reuters that the exchange is 'not leaving Europe' and would pursue authorization in another EU jurisdiction.

key_facts.fact: ESMA said unauthorized crypto firms must immediately stop onboarding new EU clients, halt marketing, and limit services to closing positions when the MiCA transition ends July 1, with possible coordinated enforcement after.
key_facts.excerpt: Unauthorized firms must immediately stop onboarding new EU clients, halt marketing activity, and limit services to what is necessary for clients to sell, transfer, or close positions. ESMA said national regulators could take coordinated enforcement action.

stories.headline: Bumble explores sale with Morgan Stanley as dating-app growth slows

key_facts.fact: Dating app Bumble is exploring a sale amid slowing growth in online dating and is working with Morgan Stanley on a potential sale process, according to three people familiar with the matter; no deal is certain.
key_facts.excerpt: Dating app Bumble is exploring a sale amid slowing growth in the online dating sector, according to three people familiar with the matter. The company... is working with investment bankers at Morgan Stanley on a potential sale process.

key_facts.fact: Total paying users fell more than 11% in full-year 2025 to about 3.7 million, while annual revenue declined nearly 10% to about $966 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Total paying users fell more than 11 per cent in the full year 2025 to about 3.7 million, while annual revenue declined nearly 10 per cent to about US$966-million.

key_facts.fact: In the first quarter of 2026, paying users dropped about 20% year-on-year after the company trimmed lower-engagement accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first quarter of 2026, paying users dropped by about 20 per cent year-on-year as the company trimmed lower-engagement accounts.

stories.headline: Otsuka's centanafadine meets primary endpoint in Phase 3b ADHD-with-anxiety trial

key_facts.fact: Otsuka announced positive topline Phase 3b results on June 25 for centanafadine XR 280 mg once daily in adults with ADHD and comorbid anxiety, meeting the primary endpoint with statistically significant and clinically relevant improvement in ADHD symptoms versus placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: Study met its primary endpoint, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically relevant improvements in ADHD symptoms in adults with ADHD and comorbid anxiety taking centanafadine compared to those taking placebo.

key_facts.fact: Centanafadine is a first-in-class norepinephrine, dopamine, and serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI).
key_facts.excerpt: Centanafadine is a first-in-class norepinephrine, dopamine, and serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI).

key_facts.fact: The drug is under FDA Priority Review for ADHD in children, adolescents and adults, with a PDUFA target action date of July 24, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Centanafadine is currently under Priority Review by the FDA for the treatment of ADHD in children, adolescents, and adults, with a target action date of July 24, 2026.
